inputs.text: The OSCE’s 2026 report isn’t simply exposing how France treats religious groups—it may be helping make that pressure seem respectable. Praising anti-antisemitism efforts while flagging “strict secularism” gives institutions cover to present scrutiny of Scientologists and Jehovah’s Witnesses as neutral vigilance. And with MIVILUDES’ lack of transparency and rulings against the state body, the public is being asked to trust institutions that resist scrutiny. That looks less like oversight than a managed narrative: acknowledge just enough to legitimize the machinery.
